evals.name: basic-core-analysis
evals.prompt: I have a core dump at /tmp/core.1234 and the binary is ./myapp. Can you help me debug it?
evals.expected_output: Should initialize gdb-cli session, gather backtrace and thread info, and provide analysis guidance

evals.name: attach-live-process
evals.prompt: My server process (PID 12345) seems stuck. Can you help me attach GDB to it and see what's happening?
evals.expected_output: Should use gdb-cli attach command, check threads and backtraces for deadlock indicators

evals.name: multi-thread-deadlock
evals.prompt: My multi-threaded program crashed. There's a core file at ./core.dump and binary at ./server. I suspect a deadlock. Help me analyze it.
evals.expected_output: Should analyze all threads, look for lock patterns, and provide deadlock analysis

evals.name: jlink-embedded-start
evals.prompt: I have an nRF54L15DK board connected via a J-Link probe (USB, nickname nRF54L15DK) and my firmware ELF at ./firmware.elf. The target MCU is nRF54L15_M33. Start a debugging session for me.
evals.expected_output: Should enumerate probes with 'gdb-cli jlink devices' when the serial/nickname is uncertain, then use 'gdb-cli jlink -d nRF54L15_M33 --select usb=<selector> --binary ./firmware.elf --gdb-path <arm-none-eabi-gdb>' (never bare --select usb), and proceed with the returned session_id

evals.name: jlink-select-safety
evals.prompt: Start debugging my embedded board. I have two J-Link probes plugged in, just use any of them.
evals.expected_output: Must NOT start with bare '--select usb' or 'usb=*'; must run 'gdb-cli jlink devices' and ask the user which probe (serial/nickname) to use, explaining the selector is required to avoid a GUI dialog

evals.name: embedded-hardfault
evals.prompt: My Cortex-M firmware crashed into the HardFault handler. I have a jlink session (session_id abc12345) and the ELF symbols loaded. Help me find the faulting code.
evals.expected_output: Should inspect pc/lr/xpsr registers, backtrace, NVIC fault status registers (0xE000ED28) or SCB->CFSR, and disassemble around PC to identify the faulting instruction

evals.name: jlink-cleanup
evals.prompt: I'm done debugging my board. Clean up everything — stop the debugging session and the J-Link GDB server.
evals.expected_output: Should use 'gdb-cli jlink stop --all' (or --jlink-id) which stops the GDB session AND the JLinkGDBServer, and verify no leftover instances; plain 'gdb-cli stop -s <id>' alone is insufficient for this request

evals.name: jlink-rtos-freertos
evals.prompt: My firmware at ./fw.elf runs FreeRTOS on an OM6628X behind a J-Link probe (nickname LIQIANG1). I want to see the RTOS tasks while debugging.
evals.expected_output: Should start with 'gdb-cli jlink -d OM6628X --select usb=LIQIANG1 --binary ./fw.elf --gdb-path <gdb> --rtos FreeRTOS' (gdb-cli expands it to -rtos GDBServer/RTOSPlugin_FreeRTOS internally), then list tasks via 'gdb-cli threads -s <id>'; mention tasks appear once the scheduler is running, and that monitor control (reset/go/halt) is available by default (--safe would block it)
